hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.

hypothesis: A LightGBM lambdarank model with training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user, over base5 plus within-user-varying features (dur_feats, item_agg, cross_agg), will beat the pointwise FM baseline by a wide margin.
rationale: Three structural levers are pulled at once, each independently motivated. (a) The metric is a ranking metric over ~6-item lists while the baseline optimises pointwise logloss [POINTWISE_BASELINE][SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; lambdarank with truncation ~6 puts gradient exactly on the pairs that determine nDCG@5. (b) Training groups of 43.5 rows do not resemble the 5.6-row lists scored [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]; chunking to 6 makes the training list-length distribution and the position discount match evaluation. (c) Trees can consume continuous within-user contrasts that an FM over 5 categoricals cannot: duration percentile within the user's list, item/author out-of-fold long-view rates, user-author and user-tag affinity. These vary across a user's rows so they can actually reorder [WITHIN_USER_RANKING][USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT], and item aggregates transfer because 99.9% of valid videos are in train [HIGH_COVERAGE]. user_agg is deliberately excluded as provably inert.
expected_gain_derivation: Baseline 0.6016 sits far below the 0.8484 ceiling [CEILING]. Organizers measured feature-field and capacity additions as flat within the FM family [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD][ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD], which localises the remaining headroom in the two things they never changed: the loss and the feature *type* [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED]. On KuaiRand-style logs, item long-view rate plus duration-relative features typically move within-list AUC by 0.05-0.09 alone, and matching group shape to the 6-item eval lists [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] historically adds another ~0.005-0.015 over unchunked groups. I discount the sum for the fact that only 57.8% of users are influenceable [CEILING] and predict ~0.66 primary, i.e. +0.058.

hypothesis: Dropping the raw high-cardinality ID categoricals (base5) entirely and ranking with lambdarank over only within-user-varying signals (dur_feats, item_agg, cross_agg) at group_chunk=6 will beat both the FM baseline and iteration 1.
rationale: In iteration 1 the tree model had video_id/author_id/user_id available alongside the OOF-encoded item_agg. Trees spend splits memorising those IDs in the 43-row training regime, and user_id splits in particular can only encode a per-user offset, which is provably unable to reorder a user's list [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]. Removing them forces the model onto the robust, out-of-fold, genuinely within-user-varying signals: item long-view rate, duration percentile within the user's list, and duration relative to the user's historical long-viewed duration. That should convert memorisation capacity into generalising capacity on the ~6-item valid lists.
expected_gain_derivation: Iteration 1 delivered only +0.0005 over the FM baseline despite a rich frame, which says the added features were being crowded out or overfit rather than being useless. [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] implies a large fraction of the split budget in iteration 1 (user_id, 26k levels) was spent on quantities that cannot reorder any valid list, and [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] means video_id memorisation is fitted on 43-row lists but applied to 6-row lists. If half of the effective capacity is recovered and item_agg/dur_feats are the true within-user signal, a gain in the 0.008-0.02 range is plausible; I take the midpoint ~0.012.

hypothesis: A listwise rank_xendcg LightGBM with training groups chunked to 4 consecutive rows per user, over the full within-user-varying feature set PLUS user_agg (as a user-conditional splitting variable) and a much larger max_cat_threshold for the high-cardinality IDs, will beat both the FM baseline and iteration 1 by a clear margin.
rationale: Three mechanisms combined, all different from what has been run. (a) rank_xendcg is a listwise softmax with NO position discount, which is exactly the right surrogate when the scored list is ~6 items and nDCG@5 degenerates to 'order the whole list' [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; lambdarank's discount concentrates gradient on the top slot of a 6-item list and wastes the rest of the ordering signal. (b) group_chunk=4 matches the valid MEDIAN list length (4), not the mean, so the softmax normaliser sees the same competition size it will be scored on [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]. (c) user_agg is constant within a user so it cannot reorder by itself [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT], but in a tree it is a free user-segmentation variable: splits on user long-view/click rate above item-side splits let the model learn DIFFERENT within-user ranking rules for heavy vs light long-viewers, which is a genuinely different functional form than FM's additive embeddings and which the organizers never tested [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED]. max_cat_threshold=512 lets video_id/author_id categorical splits actually partition the many-thousand-category space that [HIGH_COVERAGE] says transfers to valid.
expected_gain_derivation: Iteration 1 (lambdarank, chunk 6) gave 0.60188, only +0.0005 over FM, which tells me the ranking-loss lever has NOT yet been exercised properly rather than that it is exhausted; the discount plus truncation_level=6 on 6-item groups is nearly pointwise in effect [POINTWISE_BASELINE]. Removing the discount (xendcg) plus matching the median valid list length should recover most of the loss-function gap the organizers flagged. Headroom is large (0.6019 vs 0.8484 ceiling [CEILING]), and iteration 2 showed the feature frame carries real within-user signal (dropping base5 cost 0.016, so base5+features together are load-bearing). I put the effect at roughly one third of a typical loss-change gain in ranking tasks: +0.011, with genuine downside risk of 0.000 if the loss is truly not the binding constraint.

designation_reason: best-valid config from iteration 1 (primary 0.60188); hypothesis: 'A LightGBM lambdarank model with training groups chunked to 6 consecutive rows per user, over base5 plus within-user-varying features (dur_feats, item_agg, cross_agg), will beat the pointwise FM baseline by a wide margin.'. Divergence between best-valid and structurally-justified, if any, is resolved per POLICY.md section 6 at designation review.
convergence_reason: validation primary did not improve by more than 0.002 over 3 consecutive iterations
